english: Let $y:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be a differentiable function such that $x\dfrac{dy}{dx}=y\left(x+\ln y\right)$ for all $x>0$ and $y(1)=1$. Then the value of $y(3)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $y:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ एक अवकलनीय फलन है जिसके लिए सभी $x>0$ हेतु $x\dfrac{dy}{dx}=y\left(x+\ln y\right)$ तथा $y(1)=1$ है। तब $y(3)$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: The left side is $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\ln y)$, so put $u=\ln y$: $\dfrac{du}{dx}-\dfrac1xu=1$, a linear equation in $u$.
Integrating factor $\dfrac1x$: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac ux\right)=\dfrac1x$, so $\dfrac ux=\ln x+c$.
At $x=1$: $u=\ln1=0$, so $c=0$ and $u=x\ln x$. Hence $y=e^{x\ln x}=x^{x}$.
originality_note: New: an equation whose solution is y = x^x, hidden behind the substitution u = ln y (way 4). Closest known: y' = y(ln y + ...)/x textbook exercises. Different because: the forcing term x makes the linear equation give u = x ln x, which few students expect.
blueprint_concepts: Equations reducible to linear form by substitution

concept_use.Equations reducible to linear form by su: The substitution u = ln y turns the equation into the linear equation u' - u/x = 1, whose solution is u = x ln x, so y = x^x.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol and function introduced with its domain, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; y > 0 stated so ln y is defined; answer 27 is a positive 2-digit integer as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: u = ln y makes the equation linear; u = x ln x.
justification: One substitution and one integrating factor; routine. Comparable to 2023-P2-Q9 (L2).
